title: Uniqueness of the scalar-field integral closure on a connected reduced scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty connected reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Let $k_1,k_2$ be fields [def-weil-field], and let $a_i:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ be morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum] that are both locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\rho_i:k_i\to A$ for the induced ring maps; these are injective. For $i=1,2$, let $C_i\subseteq A$ be the subring of elements satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\rho_i(k_i)$ (the integral closure of $\rho_i(k_i)$ in $A$). Then $C_1=C_2$, and this common subring is a field.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), equality of the two integral closures, together with Tag 04MI (lemma-integral-closure-ground-field), asserting each integral closure is a field; nonemptiness made explicit.

proof.text: Choose a point $x\in X$. The ring $A$ is nonzero: the germ of its identity at $x$ is the nonzero identity of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Each unital map $\rho_i:k_i\to A$ is injective, since if a nonzero scalar vanished, multiplication by its image inverse would give $1=0$. Identify the fields with their images. The reducedness definition makes $A$ reduced, and [lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents] makes every idempotent of $A$ equal to zero or one.

source.place: Tag 04MI (lemma-integral-closure-ground-field), reducedness and connectedness; scalar injectivity made explicit.

proof.text: For either scalar field $k=k_i$, let $C$ be its integral closure in $A$, a subring containing $k$. For $0\ne c\in C$, [lem-sfb-reduced-integral-polynomial-generalized-inverse] gives $y=q(c)$ with $c^2y=c$. Since $y$ is a polynomial in $c$ with coefficients in $k$, it lies in $C$. The element $e=cy$ satisfies $e^2=e$. If $e=0$, then $c=ce=0$, a contradiction; hence $e=1$, and $y$ is the inverse of $c$ in $C$. Thus each $C_i$ is a field. This argument holds for every nonempty connected reduced scheme over any field, without a finite-type assumption.

source.place: Tag 04MI (lemma-integral-closure-ground-field), field conclusion, via the isolated polynomial inverse input.

proof.text: Each $C_i$ is integrally closed in $A$: if $z\in A$ is integral over $C_i$, apply [lem-sfb-integral-element-tower-descent] to $k_i\to C_i\to A$ to obtain integrality over $k_i$, hence $z\in C_i$. The inclusion $C_i\to A$ defines a morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. It is locally of finite type: choose an affine cover on which the original $k_i$-structure has finitely generated coordinate algebras; on each chart the same generators generate over $C_i$, since the chart map factors through its sections and the coefficients already contain the image of $k_i$. The new morphism composes to the original one, by the same affine-target bijection.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), quasi-compact paragraph: replacement of k_i by its integral closure, with finite type checked on the original charts.

proof.text: First suppose $X$ is quasi-compact. It is finite type over $k_1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] give finitely many irreducible components (the one affine chart of $\operatorname{Spec}k_1$ is quasi-compact and Noetherian, since a field has only the zero and unit ideals). Apply [lem-sfb-relatively-closed-constants-units-fg] with each new scalar field $C_i$: both $A^\times/C_i^\times$ are finitely generated. Put $F=C_1\cap C_2$, a field since inverses in either subfield agree in $A$. By [lem-sfb-subfield-units-quotient-finite], applied in both orders, each $C_i/F$ is finite. Thus every $c\in C_2$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $F\subseteq C_1$, so $c\in C_1$ by the relative integral closedness just proved. The reversed argument gives $C_1\subseteq C_2$. This proves equality in the quasi-compact case.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), final quasi-compact paragraph, through the two inclusions; correct final equality is C_1=C_2 (and here also F).

proof.text: For general $X$, choose the affine cover by finitely generated $k_1$-algebras in the local finite-type definition. Each chart $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence finite type over $k_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], its topology is Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open], its nonempty connected components are open, and by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] they are quasi-compact. These components, with their open subscheme structures, form an open cover $(U_j)$ of $X$ by nonempty connected reduced quasi-compact schemes. The two scalar structures remain locally finite type on these opens by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]: every affine open of an open subscheme is an affine open of $X$, so the stated coordinate-algebra condition is inherited. Apply the quasi-compact case to $U_j$: its two closures coincide in a field $K_j\subseteq\Gamma(U_j,\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), first paragraph: cover by connected quasi-compact opens. Intersections need not be affine, and their quasi-compactness is not needed in the propagation argument below.

proof.text: Let $f\in C_1$ and write $f_j=f|_{U_j}$. Restrict a monic $k_1$-equation for $f$ to see $f_j\in K_j$. Choose any index $j_0$; it exists since $X$ is nonempty and the opens cover it. As $K_{j_0}$ is also the closure of $k_2$, choose one monic polynomial $P\in k_2[T]$ with $P(f_{j_0})=0$. Let $J$ be the indices $j$ with $P(f_j)=0$. For any nonempty overlap $W=U_j\cap U_h$, the restriction maps $K_j\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ and $K_h\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ are injective: their target has $1\ne0$, as is seen at a point of $W$, and a unital map from a field to a nonzero ring is injective by the inverse argument of step 1. The restrictions of $P(f_j)$ and $P(f_h)$ agree, since restriction preserves coefficients and polynomial evaluation.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), first paragraph after the kernel display: choose a monic polynomial on one open and compare its evaluations on overlaps.

proof.text: If $j\in J$ and $U_j\cap U_h\ne\varnothing$, the equality of restrictions in step 6 and injectivity for $K_h$ imply $P(f_h)=0$, hence $h\in J$. Here $P(f_h)\in K_h$ because $k_2\subseteq K_h$. Thus the two opens $\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ and $\bigcup_{j\notin J}U_j$ are disjoint, cover $X$, and the first contains $U_{j_0}$. Connectedness forces the second to be empty. Every $U_h$ is nonempty, so every index belongs to $J$.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), propagation along a chain of overlapping opens, equivalently expressed by the open-and-closed union of successful indices.

proof.text: The section $P(f)$ restricts to zero on every $U_j$; uniqueness in the structure-sheaf gluing axiom gives $P(f)=0$ on $X$. Its polynomial is monic with coefficients in $k_2$, so $f\in C_2$. This gives $C_1\subseteq C_2$. Reversing the roles of the fields gives $C_2\subseteq C_1$. Together with step 2 this proves equality and the common-field assertion for all $X$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field), sheaf condition and propagation of the same monic polynomial. The source phrase f in k_1 here means f in its integral closure k_1'.

proof_origin.place: Tags 04MI (lemma-integral-closure-ground-field) and 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field); polynomial refinement of 04MI isolated as a new algebra lemma. The 04MK overlap-propagation argument is written using injectivity on any nonempty overlap rather than decomposing the overlap into components.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q54-7f1f7149c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole delivery: the item, all 4 new nodes and every cited statement, against Stacks varieties.tex 04MI (lemma-integral-closure-ground-field), 04MK (proposition-unique-base-field) and 04L7 (proposition-units-general, alternative 1), and Mathlib isIntegral_trans at IsIntegralClosure/Basic.lean:479. The item statement is 04MK plus 04MI's field clause, with nonempty made explicit; nothing is weakened and it is enough for the groupoid-stabilizer citer. Step 1: A is nonzero, the scalar maps are injective, A is reduced, and its only idempotents are 0 and 1. Step 2: the field clause follows from the generalized inverse, since e=cy is idempotent and c≠0 forces e=1. Step 3: the elementwise tower lemma makes C_i integrally closed in A, and X→Spec C_i is locally of finite type because the same generators work over C_i. Step 4: in the quasi-compact case X is Noetherian with finitely many components, so the 04L7 node applies with k:=C_i. The subfield node, applied both ways, makes C_1 and C_2 finite over F=C_1∩C_2, and integral closedness gives both inclusions. Step 5: the cover by connected components of Noetherian affine charts is correctly cited; the minimal condition on closed sets gives ACC on opens by complements. Steps 6-8: propagating one monic P over nonempty overlaps, using injectivity from a field into a nonzero ring and the clopen-union argument, is correct and avoids the source's unjustified finite decomposition of overlaps. I confirm the source typo: 'f in k_1' should be 'f in k_1''. Each new node is true, self-contained and not a clause of the item. Generalized inverse: tested on B=0 and on k×k with x=(1,0), proved by factoring p=T^m r and Bezout. Subfield node: the kernel is (K∩L)^×, then Laurent generators and Zariski's lemma; tested on K=L and on k(t). Units node: exact 04L7(1). Tower leaf: exact match with isIntegral_trans. Duplicate searches found nothing (04MK/04MI/04L7, units fg, absolutely flat, x^2y=x). I accept the tool uses lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents and lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open as generic black boxes. No SGA citation and no cycle. No fixes.
